title: Inference on the Smallest KL Covariate Shift Reversing a Quantile Effect Sign
banked_reason: D0.5.G rated subfield below the field floor (6.8 < 7.4), not salvageable within scope; three math and two related-work findings remain unrepaired, so mathematical soundness is not established.
gap_reasons: The near-minimum enumeration only outputs root-n competitive basins (as the expansion itself says), but \hat v_{j,n}, \hatδ_n, and \hat J_n are indexed over every population j≤m_n; permitted fixed-gap basins therefore have no estimated value, so the declared estimator/interval is not defined.

The proof standardizes every j∈\hat J_n and bounds its Gaussian half-width, but the profile theorem proves score substitution/covariance consistency only for fixed-C competitive branches; a screenable infinite-drift branch has no supplied nonzero \hatσ_{j,n} or covariance control, so c_{\hat J_n}(\hatΣ_n) and the upper-endpoint argument are not justified.

Its expectation argument needs C_n to be defined and uniformly bounded also off {\hat J_n={j_*}}, but the same unsupported standardization of noncompetitive screened branches can have \hatσ_{j,n}=0 or lack covariance consistency; the claimed uniform-integrability bound does not follow.

The closest entropy-duality comparator, BorweinLewis1991, is explicitly marked unmatched, and DonskerVaradhan1975 is not positioned; state the theorem-level relation (including the claimed no-Slater/support-face extension) or remove noncontributing citations.

Firpo2007 is cited for quantile efficiency but has no relevance/comparison sentence; position this optimized-radius canonical gradient against the fixed-QTE efficiency result rather than leaving the closest score comparator implicit.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a two-CDF entropy contact dual, a proposed uniform learned-profile expansion, and finite-contact inference, then underwent repeated D0 proof and maximality reviews. The cold D0.5 review rated the contribution subfield, below the field floor, and found no in-scope route to field. Three mathematical defects and two related-work gaps remain unrepaired; mathematical soundness was not established, and this bank entry is not a validated subfield result.
tldr: The causal target is the uncapped smallest forward-KL change in baseline-covariate composition that reverses a marginal quantile-effect sign. The minimal identification class yields an exact extended-real two-CDF dual. On the finite-contact, compact-search, globally uniform-Slater regular class, the cross-fitted estimator has a bounded-variation learned-nuisance profile expansion, tie-honest inference, and regular-oracle expected length under branch separation. A global numerical bracket uses only a directly reversing or certified strict-slack witness for its upper endpoint and an exhaustive atom-versus-continuity split for its lower endpoint; Slater is reserved for exact cap equality and inference. No Oregon empirical result is claimed because the focal-household records and computed certificates were not supplied.
gap: Published KL external-validity radii cover linear mean claims, published counterfactual-CDF methods estimate fixed shifted distributions, and published extrema methods begin with an available process approximation. None identifies and verifies the full-data-to-observed-data bridge for an optimized two-CDF radius with named learned nuisances and globally certified contacts.
fill: The project gives the exact uncapped support-face dual, derives a fixed exact computational cap from a uniform-Slater witness on the regular basins, poses the named-learner nested profile expansion as the first-class open question, derives the branch canonical gradient and finite-contact inferential consequences conditional on that expansion, and requires separate Oregon certificates for regular-subclass membership and global basin separation.
